projectCategory: DSA Module 2.3: Hashing Algorithms, Hash Maps & Collision Resolution
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms in C

projects.title: Direct Address Table (DAT) Engine
projects.description: A Direct Address Table (DAT) is the simplest hash table where keys act directly as array indices (`table[key] = value`), achieving O(1) constant search, insertion, and deletion. In this project, you will build a Direct Address Table in C for keys in range `[0..999]`. You will maintain a presence flag array to track occupied slots and handle missing keys.
projects.learningOutcome: Direct Address Tables, O(1) Absolute Lookup & Key-to-Index Mapping
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Direct Address Table (DAT) Engine ---
Key 42 found! Value = 999
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Direct Indexing**: Slot `present[key]` tracks presence; `value[key]` stores data.
2. **O(1) Time**: Insert and lookup run in 1 step without loops.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dat_insert()`: Performs direct address table insertion.

projects.title: Division Method Hash Function with Modulo Math
projects.description: When keys exceed array bounds, a Hash Function `h(k) = k % M` maps arbitrary integer keys to index positions `[0..M-1]`. Picking a prime number for table size M distributes keys uniformly and minimizes collisions. In this project, you will construct a Division Method Hash Calculator in C using a prime table size `M = 11`.
projects.learningOutcome: Division Hash Function, Modulo Arithmetic & Prime Table Size Selection
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Division Method Hash Function ---
Key  25 → Hash Index = 3
Key  42 → Hash Index = 9
Key  99 → Hash Index = 0
Key 104 → Hash Index = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Modulo Math**: `index = key % M`.
2. **Prime Modulo**: Prevents common factor clustering.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `hash_division()`: Maps key to index using division method.

projects.title: Multiplication Method Hash Function (Knuth Multiplicative Constant)
projects.description: Knuth's Multiplication Method maps key `k` using formula `h(k) = floor(M * (k * A mod 1))` where constant `A ≈ (sqrt(5) - 1) / 2 = 0.618033` (the Golden Ratio). This method works well for any table size M! In this project, you will build a Multiplicative Hash Function in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Multiplication Hashing, Knuth Golden Ratio Constant & Floating Point Hash Math
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Multiplication Method Hash Function ---
Key 123 → Hash Index = 18
Key 456 → Hash Index = 82
Key 789 → Hash Index = 62
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Fractional Part**: `frac = k * A - floor(k * A)`.
2. **Scale**: Multiply `frac` by `M` and drop decimals.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `hash_multiplication()`: Computes Knuth multiplicative hash index.

projects.title: Separate Chaining Collision Resolution using Linked Lists
projects.description: When two distinct keys produce the same hash index (`h(k1) == h(k2)`), a Collision occurs. Separate Chaining resolves collisions by turning each hash table bucket into a Singly Linked List of colliding keys. In this project, you will build a Separate Chaining Hash Table in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Collision Resolution, Separate Chaining Linked Lists & Bucket Overflow Handling
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Separate Chaining Hash Table ---
Bucket 0: NULL
Bucket 1: 36 → 29 → 22 → 15 → NULL
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Bucket Array**: `Node *table[M]` initialized to NULL.
2. **Chain Head Insert**: Prepend colliding node to `table[index]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `insert_chain()`: Inserts key into separate chaining linked list bucket.

projects.title: Open Addressing with Linear Probing Collision Resolution
projects.description: Open Addressing stores all key-value pairs directly inside the hash table array. When a collision occurs at index `h`, Linear Probing scans consecutive buckets `(h + 1) % M, (h + 2) % M ...` until an empty slot is found. In this project, you will build a Linear Probing Hash Table in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Open Addressing, Linear Probing Index Sequences & Primary Clustering Analysis
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Open Addressing Linear Probing ---
Bucket 3: 10
Bucket 4: 17
Bucket 5: 24
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Linear Scan**: Check `(hash_idx + i) % M` for `i = 0, 1, 2...`.
2. **Insert**: Place key in first empty slot `EMPTY`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `insert_linear()`: Resolves collisions via linear probing.

projects.title: Open Addressing with Quadratic Probing
projects.description: Linear Probing suffers from Primary Clustering where contiguous blocks of occupied slots grow long. Quadratic Probing uses quadratic step sequence `(h + i^2) % M` to jump over filled regions. In this project, you will build a Quadratic Probing Hash Table in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Quadratic Probing Sequence `i^2`, Eliminating Primary Clustering & Secondary Clustering
projects.exampleText: Insert colliding keys 10, 17, 24 with Quadratic Step
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Open Addressing Quadratic Probing ---
Bucket 3: 10
Bucket 4: 17
Bucket 0: 24
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Quadratic Step**: Check `(hash_idx + i * i) % M`.
2. **Scatter**: Jumps non-linearly to reduce clustering.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `insert_quadratic()`: Resolves collisions via quadratic probing.

projects.title: Double Hashing Collision Resolution Engine
projects.description: Double Hashing uses a second hash function `h2(k)` to determine step size: `(h1(k) + i * h2(k)) % M`. This eliminates both primary and secondary clustering! In this project, you will build a Double Hashing Collision Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Double Hashing Strategy, Dual Hash Functions & Secondary Clustering Elimination
projects.exampleText: Insert keys 19, 27, 36 using h1 and h2
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Double Hashing Collision Resolution ---
Bucket 5: 19
Bucket 6: 27
Bucket 1: 36
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Step Calculation**: `step = h2(k) = PRIME - (k % PRIME)`.
2. **Probe**: Check `(h1(k) + i * step) % M`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `insert_double_hash()`: Performs double hashing probe sequence.

projects.title: Hash Table Load Factor Tracker & Dynamic Rehashing
projects.description: The Load Factor `α = N / M` measures table fullness. When `α` exceeds a threshold (e.g., 0.70), collision rates surge. Dynamic Rehashing allocates a new table of double size (2M) and re-hashes all keys into the new table. In this project, you will build a Load Factor Tracker & Rehasher in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Load Factor Metrics (`α = N/M`), Dynamic Table Expansion & Amortized O(1) Rehash
projects.exampleText: Track load factor for N=8 items in M=10 capacity
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dynamic Rehashing & Load Factor Tracker ---
Items: 8, Capacity: 10, Load Factor: 0.80
--> Load Factor Threshold (0.70) Exceeded! Triggering Rehash to Capacity 20...
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Calculate Load**: `α = items / capacity`.
2. **Rehash Trigger**: If `α >= threshold`, allocate new array `capacity * 2` and re-insert items.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `check_rehash()`: Tracks load factor and triggers dynamic table expansion.

projects.title: String Hash Function (Polynomial Rolling Hash / djb2)
projects.description: Hashing strings requires converting character sequences into numeric integers. Daniel J. Bernstein's `djb2` hash algorithm uses polynomial math `hash = hash * 33 + char` to achieve excellent string distribution and low collision rates. In this project, you will build the djb2 String Hash Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: String Hashing Algorithms, djb2 Magic Constant 33 & Character Sequence Bit-Shifting
projects.exampleOutput:
--- djb2 Polynomial String Hashing ---
Hash('ANTIGRAVITY') = 698240578138
Hash('DATA_STRUCTURES') = 812948102931
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Magic Start**: Initialize `hash = 5381`.
2. **Bit-Shift**: For each char `c`: `hash = ((hash << 5) + hash) + c`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `djb2_hash()`: Computes djb2 hash value for string inputs.

projects.title: Check if Two Arrays are Disjoint using Hash Set
projects.description: Two arrays are disjoint if they share no common elements. Brute force takes O(N * M) time. Inserting Array 1 into a Hash Set and checking Array 2 elements against the Hash Set solves this in O(N + M) linear time! In this project, you will build a Disjoint Array Tester in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Hash Set Lookups, Linear O(N+M) Set Disjointness Check & Fast Element Presence Query
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Disjoint Array Tester using Hash Set ---
Arrays are completely DISJOINT (No common elements)!
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Insert Set**: Insert elements of `arr1` into boolean hash set.
2. **Check Set**: For each `arr2[i]`, if present in hash set, return false.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `is_disjoint()`: Verifies array disjointness using Hash Set in O(N+M) time.

projects.title: Two-Sum Problem in O(N) Time using Hash Map
projects.description: Given an array of integers and a target sum, find indices of two numbers that add up to target. Brute force takes O(N^2) time. Using a Hash Map storing `(number, index)` pairs solves Two-Sum in a single linear pass in O(N) time! In this project, you will build an O(N) Two-Sum Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Two-Sum Problem, Single-Pass Complement Search & Hash Map Lookup Optimization
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Two-Sum O(N) Hash Search ---
Target Sum = 9
Found Pair: 2 + 7 = 9 (Indices: 0, 1)
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Complement Check**: For `arr[i]`, compute `complement = target - arr[i]`.
2. **Lookup**: If `complement` exists in hash map, pair found; else store `hash_map[arr[i]] = i`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `two_sum()`: Solves Two-Sum problem in O(N) time using Hash Map.

projects.title: Subarray with 0 Sum Finder using Prefix Sum Hashing
projects.description: If a prefix sum repeats itself at two different array indices `i` and `j` (`PrefixSum[i] == PrefixSum[j]`), the subsegment between `i+1` and `j` MUST sum to 0! Store prefix sums in a Hash Set to find 0-sum subarrays in O(N) linear time. In this project, you will build a 0-Sum Subarray Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Prefix Sum Technique, Duplicate Prefix Detection & Zero-Sum Subarray Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Subarray with 0 Sum Finder ---
Subarray with 0 Sum EXISTS!
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Prefix Accumulate**: Maintain running `prefix_sum`.
2. **Duplicate Detection**: If `prefix_sum` seen before in hash set, 0-sum subarray exists.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `has_zero_sum_subarray()`: Detects 0-sum subarray using prefix sum hashing.

projects.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence Finder using Hash Set
projects.description: Given an unsorted array of integers, find the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence (e.g. `[1, 2, 3, 4]`). Sorting takes O(N log N) time. Using a Hash Set to find sequence starting points (`num - 1` missing in set) solves this in linear O(N) time! In this project, you will build a Longest Consecutive Sequence Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Sequence Start Point Detection, O(N) Linear Time Constraint & Hash Set Lookups
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Longest Consecutive Sequence Finder ---
Longest Consecutive Sequence Length = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Insert Set**: Insert all elements into Hash Set.
2. **Identify Starts**: If `num - 1` NOT in set, `num` is sequence start. Count consecutive steps `num + 1, num + 2...`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `longest_consecutive()`: Finds longest consecutive sequence in O(N) time.

projects.title: Group Anagrams using String Sorting & Hash Map
projects.description: Given an array of strings, group anagrams together (words containing identical letters in different orders). Sorting each string alphabetically yields a canonical key (e.g., `'eat'` → `'aet'`). Map canonical keys to lists of anagrams in a Hash Map. In this project, you will build an Anagram Grouping Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Canonical Key Generation, String Sorting Keys & Anagram Hash Table Bucketing
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Group Anagrams Hashing Engine ---
Group 1: [ eat, tea, ate ]
Group 2: [ tan, nat ]
Group 3: [ bat ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Canonical Key**: Sort string chars to create standardized key.
2. **Group Buckets**: Store words matching same sorted key in same Hash Map entry.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `group_anagrams_demo()`: Groups string anagrams using canonical hash keys.

projects.title: Find All Anagrams in a String (Sliding Window Hash Table)
projects.description: Given string S and pattern P, find all start indices of P's anagrams in S. Maintain character frequency counts of window size `len(P)` as it slides across S. In this project, you will build a Sliding Window Anagram Search Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Sliding Window Frequency Hashing, Fixed Window Frequency Checks & Anagram Locating
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Sliding Window Anagram Search ---
Anagram start indices in 'cbaebabacd': [ 0 6 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Frequency Table**: Count char frequencies of P and initial window of S.
2. **Slide Window**: Add incoming char, remove outgoing char, compare frequency arrays.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `find_anagrams()`: Finds all anagram start indices using sliding window frequency hash.

projects.title: Count Subarrays with Given Sum K using Prefix Sum Hash Map
projects.description: Find the total count of continuous subarrays whose sum equals K. Maintain running `curr_sum` and a Hash Map storing frequency of prefix sums. At each index, add `map[curr_sum - K]` to count. In this project, you will build a Subarray Sum K Counter in C in O(N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Prefix Sum Frequency Hash Map, Target Sum Complement Counting & Subarray Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Subarrays with Given Sum K ---
Total Subarrays with Sum 2 = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Prefix Sum Map**: Map stores `frequency[prefix_sum]`.
2. **Add Complement Count**: Add `prefix_map[curr_sum - K]` to total count.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `count_subarrays_with_sum()`: Counts subarrays with sum K using prefix sum hash map.

projects.title: Isomorphic Strings Validator
projects.description: Two strings S and T are Isomorphic if characters in S can be replaced to get T while preserving character order and 1-to-1 character mappings. In this project, you will build an Isomorphic Strings Validator in C using dual character mapping arrays.
projects.learningOutcome: Bi-Directional Character Mapping, Bijection Verification & Isomorphic String Checks
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Isomorphic Strings Validator ---
'egg' and 'add' → Isomorphic
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dual Mapping**: `map1[s[i]] = t[i]` and `map2[t[i]] = s[i]`.
2. **Bi-Directional Invariant**: Ensure no character maps to multiple distinct characters.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `is_isomorphic()`: Validates isomorphic string mappings.

projects.title: Minimum Index Sum of Two Lists
projects.description: Given two string lists of preferences, find common strings with the minimum index sum (`index1 + index2`). In this project, you will build a Minimum Index Sum Matcher in C using Hash Maps.
projects.learningOutcome: Preference Ranking, Dual List Index Sum Minimization & Common String Extraction
projects.exampleText: Find common restaurant with minimum index sum
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimum Index Sum of Two Lists ---
Common Restaurant with Minimum Index Sum: Shogun (Index Sum = 1)
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Map List 1**: Store `map[string] = index` for List 1.
2. **Lookup List 2**: For each item in List 2 present in map, compute `idx1 + idx2` and update min sum.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_index_sum_demo()`: Computes minimum index sum of common preference items.

projects.title: Custom LRU Cache using Doubly Linked List + Hash Map
projects.description: A Least Recently Used (LRU) Cache evicts the least recently accessed item when capacity is full. Combining a Doubly Linked List (storing items ordered by recency) with a Hash Map (storing pointer references to list nodes) achieves `get()` and `put()` in O(1) constant time! In this project, you will build an LRU Cache in C.
projects.learningOutcome: LRU Eviction Policy, Composite Data Structures (DLL + Hash Map) & O(1) Access
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Custom O(1) LRU Cache ---
Initialized Capacity 2 LRU Cache successfully.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Doubly Linked List**: Most recently used at head, least recently used at tail.
2. **Hash Map**: `hash_map[key]` points directly to list node for O(1) lookup and node moving.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `init_lru()`: Implements O(1) LRU Cache container using DLL and Hash Map.

projects.title: Custom LFU Cache (Least Frequently Used Cache Engine)
projects.description: A Least Frequently Used (LFU) Cache evicts the item with the smallest access frequency count. If a tie occurs, evict the least recently used item among them. In this project, you will build an LFU Cache Skeleton in C using frequency buckets and hash maps.
projects.learningOutcome: LFU Eviction Strategy, Access Frequency Counters & Multi-Tier Hash Table Containers
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Custom O(1) LFU Cache Engine ---
LFU Cache eviction removes least frequently used items dynamically.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Frequency Bucketing**: Store items in linked lists grouped by access frequency `min_freq`.
2. **O(1) Eviction**: Remove head item from `min_freq` list when full.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `lfu_cache_demo()`: Demonstrates LFU Cache eviction mechanics.

projects.title: Cuckoo Hashing Engine (O(1) Worst-Case Lookup with Dual Hash Tables)
projects.description: Standard open addressing hash tables take O(N) worst-case search time when collisions cascade. Cuckoo Hashing guarantees worst-case O(1) lookup time by maintaining TWO hash tables with two distinct hash functions `h1(k)` and `h2(k)`. If a collision occurs, kick out the existing key to its alternate hash table location! In this project, you will build a Cuckoo Hashing Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Cuckoo Hashing Mechanics, Dual Hash Tables, Absolute O(1) Worst-Case Lookup & Kickout Cycles
projects.exampleText: Insert keys 20, 50, 53 into Cuckoo Hash Tables
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Cuckoo Hashing O(1) Worst-Case Engine ---
Inserted keys into dual Cuckoo hash tables successfully.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dual Locations**: Key must reside at `table1[h1(k)]` or `table2[h2(k)]`.
2. **Kickout Loop**: If slot occupied, evict existing key and move to its alternate table.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `cuckoo_insert()`: Implements Cuckoo Hashing with dual table kickout displacement.

projects.title: Robin Hood Hashing Engine (Distance-to-Initial-Bucket Equalization)
projects.description: Robin Hood Hashing is an open addressing variant that minimizes variance in probe sequence length. When inserting a new key, if the new key's Probe Distance to Initial Bucket (PSL) is larger than the existing key's PSL, swap keys ('take from the rich, give to the poor'). In this project, you will build a Robin Hood Hashing Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Robin Hood Probe Equalization, PSL (Probe Sequence Length) Metrics & Variance Reduction
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Robin Hood Hashing Engine ---
Robin Hood probing steals slots from rich entries to equalize probe distance.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **PSL Metric**: Track distance from `ideal_hash_index`.
2. **Swap Rich**: If `new_key.PSL > existing_key.PSL`, swap keys and continue probing with evicted key.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `robin_hood_demo()`: Demonstrates Robin Hood probe sequence length equalization.

projects.title: Consistent Hashing Ring for Distributed Cache Cluster
projects.description: In distributed databases (Memcached, Cassandra), adding/removing a server node invalidates standard modulo hash tables `k % N`. Consistent Hashing maps both servers and data keys onto a 360-degree hash ring `[0..2^32-1]`. When nodes are added/removed, only `1/N` keys are remapped! In this project, you will build a Consistent Hashing Ring Simulator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Distributed System Hashing, Hash Ring Topology & Virtual Server Nodes
projects.exampleText: Map key 'user_102' on Consistent Hash Ring
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Consistent Hashing Ring for Distributed Clusters ---
Key 'user_102' mapped to Server Node 2 (Hash Ring Angle 120 deg)
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Hash Ring**: Map servers and keys to integer ring range.
2. **Clockwise Assignment**: Data key assigned to first server encountered moving clockwise on ring.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `consistent_hashing_demo()`: Simulates consistent hashing ring for distributed cache nodes.

projects.title: Counting Bloom Filter with Deletion Support
projects.description: Standard Bloom Filters use bit arrays to test set membership in O(K) time with zero false negatives, but CANNOT delete items. A Counting Bloom Filter replaces single bits with 4-bit integer counters, incrementing on insert and decrementing on delete! In this project, you will build a Counting Bloom Filter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Probabilistic Data Structures, Counting Bloom Filters & Element Deletion Mechanics
projects.exampleText: Insert item 42 into Counting Bloom Filter
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Counting Bloom Filter with Deletion Support ---
Inserted item 42 into Counting Bloom Filter.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Multi-Hash**: Run K independent hash functions.
2. **Counter Array**: Increment `counts[h_i(x)]++` on insert; decrement on delete.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bloom_insert()`: Implements Counting Bloom Filter insertions.

projects.title: Lock-Free Parallel Hash Table (Atomic CAS Collision Resolution)
projects.description: High-throughput multi-threaded web servers require parallel hash tables that avoid mutex locks. Using atomic CPU Compare-And-Swap (`CAS`) instructions, concurrent threads insert keys safely into open addressing slots without thread blocking. In this project, you will build a Lock-Free Parallel Hash Table Simulator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Lock-Free Multithreading, Atomic CPU Compare-And-Swap (CAS) & High-Concurrency Hash Tables
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Lock-Free Parallel Hash Table (Atomic CAS) ---
Atomic compare-and-swap (CAS) resolved collision concurrently without mutex locks.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Atomic CAS**: `__sync_val_compare_and_swap(&table[i], EMPTY, new_key)`.
2. **Lock-Free**: If CAS succeeds, key inserted; if CAS fails, advance probe index.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `lock_free_hash_demo()`: Demonstrates atomic CAS lock-free hash table operations.
